rounds.text: Minda Corporation Ltd is clearly under-appreciated by the broader market, evidenced by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 850 per share against a market price of Rs 701, offering a 17.6% margin of safety [E46, E47]. The business demonstrates exceptional operational momentum, with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth surging at 27% [E17] and compounded profit growth hitting an impressive 57% [E21]. Furthermore, profitability is backed by reality rather than accounting tricks, as evidenced by a stellar cash conversion ratio of 1.89x with operating cash flow reaching Rs 676 Cr in March 2026, which fully backs reported profits at 110% [E34, E35, E37]. Institutional confidence is fundamentally expanding, shown by foreign institutions increasing their stake by 3.77 percentage points to 9.30% and domestic institutions raising theirs by 4.67 percentage points to 17.87% since September 2023 [E43, E44]. Adding to this strength, a rules-based screen awards the company a high score of 89 out of 100 with a BUY rating, supported by sector tailwinds in Automobile and Auto Components carrying a positive score of 0.63 [E63, E70, E72]. Conceded: [E2], [E7], [E11], [E39], [E60], [E61], [E62].

Minda Corporation Ltd carries notable valuation and structural risks despite its recent top-line expansion. The stock trades at an elevated trailing P/E of 41.6x and a P/B of 6.37x (₹ 701 on a book value of ₹ 110), significantly outpacing sector benchmarks where the sector P/B is 2.8x and EV/EBITDA stands at 19.67x against a sector benchmark of 12.62x [E1, E2, E7, E11, E60]. Furthermore, the company exhibits a low return on equity of 13.3% over the last 3 years and an ROCE of 12.27% that trails the sector benchmark of 12.54% [E10, E61]. Short-term liquidity appears constrained as the current ratio sits at 0.94x, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E39]. Institutional money flow reads negative with a holding change of -0.45 percentage points, accompanied by recent institutional outflow flags [E45, E69]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is 21%, profit growth over the trailing twelve months is 57%, and the rules-based screen scores 89 out of 100 [E15, E21, E63].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E7, E11, E10, E39, E45, E60, E61, E69]. While multiples are high, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 850 per share against the market price of Rs 701, providing a solid margin of safety [E46, E47]. The reverse DCF shows that the current price only implies a 15.3% growth rate, which is easily cleared by the company's 21% 5-year sales growth, 57% trailing profit growth, and recent rules-based score of 89 out of 100 [E15, E21, E48, E63]. Furthermore, operational quality is high with cash conversion at 1.89x, operating cash flow reaching Rs 676 Cr, and profits fully backed by cash [E34, E35, E37]. Institutional conviction remains broad despite short-term flow signals, as foreign and domestic institutions have expanded their holdings significantly since late 2023 [E43, E44]. Finally, the overarching macro backdrop strongly supports the valuation setup through an active sector tailwind score of +0.63 in Automobile and Auto Components [E70, E72].

Conceded: [E34, E35, E37, E43, E44, E70, E72]. While cash flows and institutional long-term accumulation are present, the bull relies on a DCF model [E46, E47, E48] that is heavily contradicted by severe valuation and liquidity risks. The stock trades at an elevated P/E of 41.6x [E1] and a Price-to-Book ratio of 6.37x against a sector benchmark of 2.8x [E2, E7], alongside an EV/EBITDA of 19.67x that far exceeds the 12.62x sector benchmark [E11]. Furthermore, the current ratio sits at 0.94x, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E39], while ROCE of 12.27% trails the 12.54% sector benchmark [E10] and 3-year average ROE is low at 13.3% [E61]. The bull's reliance on reverse DCF growth assumptions ignores historical volatility marked by a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.3% [E54], and recent institutional money flow reads negative [E45], signaling near-term distribution by smart money despite multi-year holding gains.

Conceded: [E7, E11, E39, E54]. While the bear cites a trailing ROCE slightly below sector benchmarks [E10], the company's ROA of 7.52% outperforms the sector benchmark of 6.04% [E8], and its cash conversion of 1.89x with operating cash flow backing profits at 110% proves the business generates pristine cash quality [E34, E37]. The DCF intrinsic value of Rs 850 per share provides a legitimate 17.6% margin of safety over the market price [E46, E47]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price requires a 15.3% growth rate, which is well supported by the company's historical 5-year profit growth of 31% and sales growth of 21% [E15, E19, E48]. Finally, institutional accumulation since September 2023 shows strong long-term sponsorship, with foreign holding up 3.77 percentage points and domestic holding up 4.67 percentage points, outweighing short-term distribution signals [E43, E44, E45].

Conceded: [E8]. While the bull leans on ROA to mask return deficits, the company's ROCE of 12.27% still lags behind the sector benchmark of 12.54% [E10], and its 3-year average ROE sits at a low 13.3% [E61]. The bull's reliance on cash conversion overlooks the severe liquidity warning that current liabilities exceed current assets with a current ratio of only 0.94x [E39]. The 17.6% margin of safety and reverse DCF assumptions are undermined by the reality that the stock price has outpaced fundamental profit growth over a 5-year span, running as a price-led move [E47, E48, E57]. Furthermore, pointing to long-term institutional sponsorship ignores the active short-term data showing negative money flow with an institutional holding change of -0.45 percentage points [E43, E44, E45]. Finally, any past growth figures must be weighed against a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.3% and an inconsistent operating margin trend over the last year [E32, E54].
